channel.title: Signal & Noise Public
channel.description: Signal & Noise is a podcast curated by Augusto Restrepo. Each episode takes a topic he's been following — articles, posts, research and conversations he curates from across the web — and double-clicks on it. Max, the optimist, makes the bull case; Lena, the skeptic, pokes holes in it. Together they separate the signal from the noise, so the big ideas are easier to understand and judge. Casual, curious, and grounded in facts.

item.title: Nautilus Q3: Foundation Year, Raise Pending
item.description:
Nautilus Biotechnology (NAUT) reported Q3 2026 results on October 27. Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) go through the numbers, the Voyager launch timeline, and the analyst Q&A: who asked what, what management committed to, and what it dodged.
In this episode: - Q3: revenue $234K (grant $208K + service $26K), net loss $15.6M ($0.12/share), cash and investments $114.3M, runway guided into Q1 2028 - Roadmap: first beta instrument this year, AKT1 Early Access late 2026, pre-orders early 2027, instrument shipments mid-2027 - Oncology assays (AKT1, EGFR, P53) matching tau-level reproducibility after about a year of development - Q&A with Guggenheim, TD Cowen, Roth Capital and a fourth analyst: customer counts not disclosed, instrument price not final, "27 is a year where we set the foundation and 28 is a year where we really go and scale the business" - Not asked by any analyst: the planned capital raise before mid-2027, and Early Access pricing and margins - Call-ins on instrument buying and on financing
Sources: Nautilus press release (Oct 27, 2026), Benzinga call transcript, Form 8-K (Sep 11, 2026), Investing.com, market quotes as of about 10 AM ET. Management quotes are verbatim from the transcript. Social posts are paraphrased.
Callers Ruth and Kit are fictional characters, and their comments are illustrative. This is not investment advice.
Chapters: 1. Beat, dip, rip; 2. The numbers; 3. The roadmap; 4. The Q&A; 5. Call-ins: the lab and the money; 6. The tape and the chatter; 7. Verdict.

item.title: Anthropic Files Its S-1 — $16B Revenue, an $81B Paper Loss & a One-Share Founder Vote
item.description: Special edition: Anthropic publicly filed its S-1 on Oct 26, 2026 (Nasdaq: ANT; Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley lead). Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) go through the filing: $16.3B H1 revenue (+1,304%), the $80.7B GAAP loss (mostly convertible-note revaluation), Q2 operating profit, $265.6B in purchase commitments and $321.4B in leases, the SpaceX, Microsoft, Amazon and Google deals, the LTBT, Founder LLC (50.1% vote) governance, market reaction, OpenAI, and read-across to the AI Infrastructure, AI Verticals and Musk theses. There is no price range or share count yet. Valuation ($1.5–2T) and timing (~Nov 19–20) come from press reports, not the filing. Graham and Wanjiru are fictional call-in characters. Sources: SEC EDGAR S-1, Anthropic, CNBC live, Reuters/Investing.com, CoinDesk, Yahoo Finance, Stock Titan.

item.title: All-In This Week: Cyber Panic, Griffin's Bubble, France at Five Percent — Max vs Lena
item.description:
An unofficial recap of the past week of the All-In podcast (Chamath Palihapitiya, Jason Calacanis, David Sacks and David Friedberg), Oct 17–24, 2026. It covers all three All-In releases since last week's recap: the main show, episode 294, "AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?" (released Oct 23, 7:08 PM ET), and two interviews: Figma CEO Dylan Field (Oct 19, 4:43 PM ET) and IBM's Arvind Krishna with Palo Alto Networks' Nikesh Arora (Oct 21, 7:42 PM ET). Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) go topic by topic.
Topics: Ken Griffin's bubble warning and Chamath's "negative free cash flow" AI spend argument, the Ramp spend data and the early-AWS analogy; open-weight versus frontier models, explainability and resilient inference; the PHP vulnerability scare (only CVE IDs leaked, per the PHP Foundation) and what defenders should do; agents, banks and who carries liability, including "abliterated" models; tech debt, security budgets, Mythos, Arvind's three war lessons and pooled vulnerability sharing; the quantum clock; Dylan Field on whether AI is killing SaaS, vertical integration, Figma's growth, the "AI psychosis moment" and the OpenAI math result; data-center bans and labor versus capital; France's riots, the 10-year above 5% and the spread versus Germany; the fixes, a SpaceX share for every kid, and the minimum wage fight.
Made-up call-ins: Walt, a fictional incident responder, and Colette, a fictional bond strategist. Both are invented for this episode and speak for no real person or firm.
Sources: public Podscripts transcripts of all three episodes; official episode titles and release times (All-In RSS); public PHP Foundation, Wiz and CISA notices on the PHP vulnerabilities; public market coverage of French bond yields, spreads and Moody's. Speaker attributions are inferred from context; where unclear we say "one of them". Numbers are rounded and are the speakers' claims unless flagged. Hosts don't imitate the besties' voices. Not affiliated with All-In; not investment advice.
Chapters: 1. This week on All-In; 2. Ken Griffin's bubble warning; 3. Open weights versus frontier models; 4. Cyber panic: the PHP bugs; 5. Call-in: Walt, a fictional incident responder; 6. Agents, banks and who pays; 7. Tech debt, budgets and the narrative problem; 8. The quantum clock; 9. Is AI killing software? Dylan Field and the SaaS question; 10. Data center bans and labor versus capital; 11. France: riots and the bond market; 12. Call-in: Colette, a fictional bond strategist; 13. The fixes, a SpaceX share for every kid, and the minimum wage fight; 14. Wrap and what to watch.

item.title: All-In This Week: CoreWeave's Bond Scare — Max vs Lena
item.description:
An unofficial recap of the past week of the All-In podcast (Chamath Palihapitiya, Jason Calacanis, David Sacks and David Friedberg), Oct 10–17, 2026. It covers all three All-In episodes released since last week's recap: the main show, episode 293, "CoreWeave Crash, AI Trade Cracks, Anthropic IPO Red Flags, Bill Gates Doomer" (released Oct 16, 9:51 PM ET; Ben Horowitz fills in for Friedberg), and two All-In Summit interviews: "Martin Shkreli: Big Pharma's Blind Spot, Betting Against Quantum & What Prison Taught Him" (Oct 12, 11:49 AM ET) and "Elizabeth Holmes' Husband Billy Evans: The Trial, Prison & Nathan Fielder's Documentary" with Friedberg (Oct 14, 9:54 PM ET). Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) go topic by topic.
Topics: CoreWeave's bond and CDS selloff, Chamath's credit math and "reflexive loop", Sacks' volatility-not-fundamentals case and the 9.6% coupon point; Ben Horowitz's Loudcloud bandwidth story, Sacks' payback-period metric (CoreWeave vs SpaceX), spot vs contract pricing and liquidated damages; power as the moat ("get long energy"); AI's deflationary effect on software and the "Jevons paradox of software"; Anthropic's investor-day numbers, Chamath's case for a $200–250B raise, the "defensive hedge" framing, OpenAI governance and Sam Altman's equity; "Psyop Corner" on Anthropic's IoT-worm and distillation posts, Coinbase's small fraud model, and the constitution-rewriting paper; the Bill Gates "doomer" segment (strong opinions flagged as such) and Ali Ghodsi's four preconditions for runaway self-improvement; Martin Shkreli on quantum computing, photonics, drug-rights arbitrage, AI drug discovery and prison; Billy Evans on meeting Elizabeth Holmes, the trial, sentencing math (his claims), the on-stage call from prison, the Nathan Fielder documentary and his Raman-spectroscopy startup.
Made-up call-ins: Morag, a fictional Glasgow-born leveraged-finance analyst, and Lachlan, a fictional Sydney embedded-device security researcher. Both are invented for this episode and speak for no real person or firm.
Sources: the official All-In episode descriptions and timestamps (libsyn RSS / Apple Podcasts); public Podscripts transcripts of the Shkreli and Evans interviews; our own machine transcript of episode 293's audio (no public transcript was available yet), cross-checked against public write-ups; CNBC coverage of the Oct 14 CoreWeave selloff; public X posts by Antonio Linares and Raoul Pal. Speaker attributions are inferred from context; where unclear we say "one of them". Numbers are rounded and are the speakers' claims. Hosts don't imitate the besties' voices. Not affiliated with All-In; not investment advice.
Chapters: 1. This week on All-In; 2. CoreWeave's bond scare: did the AI bubble pop?; 3. Call-in: Morag, a fictional credit analyst; 4. Ben's bandwidth scar, payback periods, and spot vs. contract; 5. Power is the moat: "get long energy"; 6. Decompiled software and the Jevons paradox; 7. Anthropic's investor day: $16.8 billion and a fuzzy growth rate; 8. Psyop Corner: AI worms, distillation, and small models; 9. Call-in: Lachlan, a fictional IoT security researcher; 10. Understanding Bill Gates the doomer; 11. Martin Shkreli: shorting quantum, cheap molecules, and prison; 12. Billy Evans: Elizabeth Holmes, the trial, and the phone call; 13. Scorecard: bull vs. bear for the week.

item.title: All-In This Week: Is Claude Conscious? — Max vs Lena
item.description:
An unofficial recap of the past week of the All-In podcast (Chamath Palihapitiya, Jason Calacanis, David Sacks and David Friedberg), Oct 3–10, 2026. Only one All-In episode was released since last week's recap: the main show, episode 292, "Is Claude Conscious? Pope Rejects, Model Welfare Movement, OpenAI's Math Backlash, France Riots" (released Oct 9, 10:06 PM ET). Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) go topic by topic.
Topics: the New York Times report on Anthropic hosting religious leaders on Claude's possible consciousness and the Vatican episode; Friedberg's "birth of a new religion" view and Chamath's Descartes steelman; Sacks on the Claude Constitution's "conscientious objector" language and a played Mustafa Suleyman clip (the "epistemic hall of mirrors"); market vs. externalities, Chamath's three goals of alignment, and Roko's Basilisk; OpenAI's 700+ math papers, the "loops" idea, verifiability, and Chamath's pushback; the missing cryptography results (speculation) and expert gatekeeping; France's strikes and riots, Friedberg's "socialism point of guaranteed return", Sacks on subsidies; bond vigilantes, debt-to-GDP and yields; headless agents (Grok Bot, Dots), and Chamath's "software IP is worthless" claim.
Made-up call-ins: Callum, a fictional Dublin philosophy-of-mind researcher, and Graham, a fictional Manchester bond strategist. Both are invented for this episode and speak for no real person or firm.
Sources: the official All-In episode description and timestamps (libsyn RSS / Apple Podcasts), our own machine transcript of the episode audio (no public transcript was available yet), cross-checked against a public write-up. Speaker attributions are inferred from context; where unclear we say "one of them". Numbers are rounded and are the speakers' claims. Hosts don't imitate the besties' voices. Not affiliated with All-In; not investment advice.
Chapters: 1. This week on All-In; 2. Anthropic, the Pope and a new religion; 3. The conscientious objector clause; 4. Call-in: Callum on minds and machines; 5. Let the market sort it? And Roko's Basilisk; 6. OpenAI's math dump; 7. The missing crypto proofs, and who guards the frontier; 8. France and the socialism point of guaranteed return; 9. Bond vigilantes, plus a call-in; 10. Headless agents and the end of software IP?; 11. What it all means.

item.title: All-In This Week: White House AI Accord — Max vs Lena
item.description:
An unofficial recap of the past week of the All-In podcast (Chamath Palihapitiya, Jason Calacanis, David Sacks and David Friedberg), Sep 30–Oct 2, 2026. Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) go topic by topic through both episodes released after last week's Daniel Ek interview: the Summit interview "Jake Paul & The Chainsmokers: Turning Fame into Funds, Jake Enters Politics? & Venture Bubble Signs" (Sep 30), and the main show, episode 291, "Trump's Super Intelligence Summit, AI Safety Accord, GDP Beats, Midterm Predictions" (Oct 2).
Topics: the White House Super Intelligence Summit and voluntary AI safety accord (six frontier labs, external audits, board fiduciary duty, D&O teeth); cybersecurity arms race and data centers as national security; America.gov and coordinated "doomer" messaging; GDP/jobs/inflation beats versus diesel, rates and a late-October bank-impairment warning; midterm and 2028 predictions; media coverage of the attempted Dubai–Tel Aviv hijacking; Jake Paul's attention-as-capital thesis, MVP vs UFC, and politics ambitions; The Chainsmokers on music-to-venture, sixth-man investing, DPI and bubble tells.
Made-up guests: Mara, a fictional Vancouver AI governance lawyer, joins in the Accord chapter. Finn, a fictional Auckland creator-economy investor, joins in the Jake Paul chapter. Both are invented for this episode and speak for no real firm.
Sources: the official All-In episode descriptions and timestamps (Apple Podcasts / iTunes lookup), and published episode transcripts (Podscripts) for both episodes, cross-checked against a public write-up of episode 291. Hosts only describe what the besties said, and they don't imitate their voices. Where a transcript didn't make clear who said something, we say "one of them". item.description:
An unofficial recap of the past week of the All-In podcast (Chamath Palihapitiya, Jason Calacanis, David Sacks and David Friedberg), Sep 21–29, 2026. Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) go topic by topic through all six episodes released that week: the main show, episode 290 ("Anthropic IPO at Risk, Meta's Muse Pop, Token Prices Fall, Open Source Gains Share, Alignment Fails", Sep 25), plus the Summit and interview episodes with Naveen Rao (Sep 21), Blake Scholl (Sep 22), Steve Hilton & Spencer Pratt (Sep 22), Luca Ferrari (Sep 23) and Daniel Ek (Sep 28).
Topics: "labs" vs. companies and product liability; the flood of open-weight models and the claimed flip in token share; whether Anthropic's IPO is in trouble (Polymarket odds, super-voting shares, Chamath's "$1 trillion or less" math, Sacks' "stable duopoly on a hamster wheel"); Bernie Sanders' superintelligence bill, Trump, Bessent and Obama; Meta's Muse, agents and the App Store's 30% cut; alignment, Claude's constitution and Anthropic's wet lab; AI's energy wall (Naveen Rao's dynamical computer, Boom's jet engines for data centers); Bending Spoons' buy-and-fix model; California's governor race; and Daniel Ek's $499 Neko Health scan.
Made-up guest: Dev, a fictional quant, joins briefly in the Anthropic chapter. He is invented for this episode and speaks for no real fund.
Sources: the official All-In episode descriptions and timestamps (RSS feed and YouTube), published episode transcripts (Happy Scribe) for five episodes, and our own Whisper transcription of the Daniel Ek episode's audio, cross-checked against published summaries. Hosts only describe what the besties said, and they don't imitate their voices. Where a transcript didn't make clear who said something, we say "one of them". Numbers are rounded and are the speakers' claims (for example valuations, Polymarket odds, token-share charts and company stats) unless we say otherwise. This is not affiliated with All-In and is not investment advice.

An unofficial recap of the past week of the All-In podcast (Chamath Palihapitiya, Jason Calacanis, David Sacks and David Friedberg), Sep 21–29, 2026. Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) go topic by topic through all six episodes released that week: the main show, episode 290 ("Anthropic IPO at Risk, Meta's Muse Pop, Token Prices Fall, Open Source Gains Share, Alignment Fails", Sep 25), plus the Summit and interview episodes with Naveen Rao (Sep 21), Blake Scholl (Sep 22), Steve Hilton & Spencer Pratt (Sep 22), Luca Ferrari (Sep 23) and Daniel Ek (Sep 28).
Topics: "labs" vs. companies and product liability; the flood of open-weight models and the claimed flip in token share; whether Anthropic's IPO is in trouble (Polymarket odds, super-voting shares, Chamath's "$1 trillion or less" math, Sacks' "stable duopoly on a hamster wheel"); Bernie Sanders' superintelligence bill, Trump, Bessent and Obama; Meta's Muse, agents and the App Store's 30% cut; alignment, Claude's constitution and Anthropic's wet lab; AI's energy wall (Naveen Rao's dynamical computer, Boom's jet engines for data centers); Bending Spoons' buy-and-fix model; California's governor race; and Daniel Ek's $499 Neko Health scan.
Made-up guest: Dev, a fictional quant, joins briefly in the Anthropic chapter. He is invented for this episode and speaks for no real fund.
Sources: the official All-In episode descriptions and timestamps (RSS feed and YouTube), published episode transcripts (Happy Scribe) for five episodes, and our own Whisper transcription of the Daniel Ek episode's audio, cross-checked against published summaries. Hosts only describe what the besties said, and they don't imitate their voices. Where a transcript didn't make clear who said something, we say "one of them". Numbers are rounded and are the speakers' claims (for example valuations, Polymarket odds, token-share charts and company stats) unless we say otherwise. This is not affiliated with All-In and is not investment advice.
Chapters: 1. This week on All-In; 2. They're not labs, they're companies; 3. The open-source flood; 4. Is Anthropic's IPO in trouble?; 5. Bernie, Trump, Obama and the politics of AI; 6. Muse, agents and the App Store's thirty percent; 7. Alignment, Claude's constitution and the wet lab; 8. The energy wall: Naveen Rao and Boom's jet engines; 9. Bending Spoons: buying product-market fit; 10. California: Steve Hilton and Spencer Pratt; 11. Daniel Ek, Neko and the body scan; 12. What we'd watch next.
item.itunes:author: Augusto Restrepo

item.title: Biology Eats the Market — Max vs Lena (Special)
item.description:
A one-off special. Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) debate Antonio Linares's "bio/acc basket": his claim that biology drives most market returns over the next decade, and his four picks. Nautilus (NAUT) reads the proteome, Recursion (RXRX) designs drugs with A.I., ImmunityBio (IBRX) reboots the immune system with Anktiva, and MiNK Therapeutics (INKT) takes iNKT cell therapy after solid tumors. Max makes the case from the post and its 33-minute video: biology becomes code, a read, design, reboot and strike stack, disciplined management teams, and pharma money already flowing into Recursion. Lena pushes back with the latest filings: Nautilus's first revenue of about $0.2M and its Broadscale delay, Recursion's cash burn, ImmunityBio's 45x sales valuation and the FDA warning letter, and MiNK's roughly $9M cash plus a 17-patient phase 2 with zero responses. A made-up guest, Nigel, drops by to heckle the whole idea of "platform" biotech.
Source (credit): Antonio Linares (@alc2022) on X, Sep 28, 2026, https://x.com/alc2022/status/2104620231922745534 (post and attached video). Also referenced: Q2 2026 results and filings from Nautilus, Recursion, ImmunityBio and MiNK; ImmunityBio's FDA warning letter and PDUFA date; MiNK's AACR 2026 phase 2 poster; market prices as of the Sep 28, 2026 close. Numbers are rounded. The hosts flag claims they couldn't verify on air. Nigel is fictional. This is not investment advice.
Chapters: 1. Biology is the new compute; 2. Read it, then design it; 3. Reboot and strike; 4. A stack or four lottery tickets?.
